title: CLO2024.1 - Improvement of Measurement Points (POM)
description: CLO2024.1 New Version Fully Upgraded! You can now apply measurement points according to the outer contour of the fabric piece, or freely create measurement points inside and outside the fabric piece. Click the video to see details.
transcript:
From version 2024.1, we have improved the measurement point function, enabling measurements within this version.  
In this video, let's learn in detail how to use the measurement point tool.  
Now, when you select the measurement point tool, you will automatically enter the mode for measuring line length.  
You can see that the mouse pointer at this time will be the same deep red as the inner line.  
We can use it to measure straight line distances on the board, curve distances, and multi-line distances.  
The text next to the progress bar provides prompts.  
Pressing the P key will switch to measuring the length of the measurement board.  
Press the P key to switch modes.  
At this point, you can see the mouse pointer changes to blue and the prompt updates.  
Press the P key again to switch to measuring the length of straight lines and lines.  
The translation for the current version has not been updated yet and will be corrected later.  
Press the P key again to switch back.  
Let's first learn the line length measurement mode.  
To use this tool, press the start button.  
During measurement, you can press multi-line measurement again.  
Double-click to finish.  
You can also press the Control key to create a curve.  
Double-click to finish.  
The operation is exactly the same as for the inner line.  
The latest version allows you to start and end measurements at any position on the board.  
We can also use the edit measurement point tool to move and edit measurement points.  
If a measurement point is not needed, we can delete it.  
First, let's measure the length of the front piece, that is, the front palm of the garment.  
Press the Shift key to constrain vertical direction.  
Double-click to finish.  
You will see a new measurement point appear in the window on the right side of the object.  
Since this board includes code information, all size data of the pattern can be obtained at once.  
Then we can modify its name.  
You can also use this mode to measure the distance from the top to the end of the board—for example, measuring the width of the front.  
If you find that the measured line is a virtual line and the displayed size in the object window is zero,  
then you need to switch to the edit measurement point tool, select this measurement line,  
right-click to display the length.  
Finally, use it to measure the chest width.  
It can be used to measure the width of the board.  
Press the start button.  
Press the middle mouse button.  
Press the Shift key to constrain horizontal direction.  
Double-click to finish.  
You can also use this mode.  
We need to move to the correct position.  
Press the left mouse button to change the direction of the board.  
If you see that the position exactly matches your foot’s position,  
press the start button to change the direction.  
We can input a specific value to achieve precise positioning in the image.  
Press the start button.  
Press the right mouse button while moving.  
Then click the specific data input window.  
Click OK.  
Click OK again.  
Then we will switch the texture surface—  
the top left of our post—to our previous point,  
then switch back to the black and white surface.  
Next, press the P key to switch to measuring the length of the outside of the board.  
The way to use this tool is the same anywhere on the outside of the board:  
single-click to start, single-click to end, and the free sewing tool works the same.  
Then we can measure the length of the T-stitch embroidery mountain curve.  
We return to a bit of information on the positions just measured  
to make another course.  
In addition to this tool,  
there are also manufacturing tools.  
Besides measuring curves, we can also use the hook and loop tool to measure curves.  
Select the pre-sew dragon curve and right-click to hook it as a measurement point.  
You can also measure the distance of this curve.  
Now we switch to the edit measurement tool and select the pre-sew dragon right-click point we just measured.  
We can see the menu selection.  
Select the straight line length.  
The current line is the length value of the T-shape.  
Thus, we can switch between the two measurements.  
We can also see the length of the X-shape and the length of the Y-shape  
and reverse them.  
Finally, switch back to the straight line length.  
We can see that all measured values are displayed as corresponding lines in the 3D garment.  
If we need to hide them, we can hide them in the garment information display.  
We can hide them in the 2D size display.  
If we want, we can also hide them in the 3D size display.  
In the object window, this corresponds to the length of a 3D line.  
Select this option.  
You can check the length of the 3D line in the object window.  
In the property editor, you can check the length difference between the 2D and 3D lines.  
What causes the difference?  
It is because the garment has been simulated,  
subject to fabric stretch under gravity,  
and some effects of the artificial structure and the model wearing it.  
There will be a certain degree of deformation.  
Finally, let’s look at storing and using measurement data.  
After editing measurement data that needs to be stored,  
use the storage button in the upper right corner of the object window.  
The measurement data will be saved into a CSV file.  
This file is a table-format file.  
Use office software to open and check it.  
When we need to measure new styles,  
you can directly open this style.  
At this time, we can go to the measurement point in the object window,  
open the previously saved CSV file,  
and see that the measurement positions are already set in the object window.  
There is no need to fill them in each time.  
Switch to the measurement tool.  
Select the position we need to measure.  
Press at the length position.  
Make sure there is a contrast displayed in front,  
proving that we have chosen the corresponding position.  
Then measure.  
Press start.  
Double-click to finish.  
We can measure the position,  
which can be filled directly into the blue field.  
If we need to measure new positions,  
you can also directly click to add them.  
Fill in the position to be measured first,  
then measure.  
Finally, let’s look at the application button at the bottom.  
We can choose our data,  
then click apply.  
It will be filled into the required column.  
The above is an introduction to all measurement tools.  
I hope you can use this function better in the course.

chunks.content: ## Overview of Measurement Point Function in CLO2024.1 This section introduces the enhanced measurement point function in CLO2024.1, which allows precise measurement of lines and curves on garment patterns. Key terms include measurement point tool, line length measurement, curve measurement, and edit measurement point tool. --- ## Measurement Point Tool Modes and Usage The measurement point tool automatically enters line length measurement mode upon selection, indicated by a deep red mouse pointer matching the inner line color. Users can measure straight lines, curves, and multi-line distances on the pattern board. - **Switching Modes:** Pressing the **P key** cycles through different measurement modes: - Measurement of inner line lengths (red pointer) - Measurement of outside board lengths (blue pointer) - Back to inner line length measurement The prompt text next to the progress bar updates accordingly (note: translation updates are pending). - **Basic Operations:** - Press **Start** to begin measurement. - For multi-line measurements, press the multi-line measurement option again. - Double-click to finish measurement. - Hold **Control** key to create curved measurements. - Measurements can start and end at any position on the pattern board. --- ## Editing and Managing Measurement Points The **edit measurement point tool** allows users to move, modify, or delete existing measurement points. - To delete a measurement point, select it and remove it via the edit tool. - Measurement points appear in a dedicated window on the right side of the interface. - Users can rename measurement points for clarity. --- ## Measuring Specific Garment Dimensions Examples using the measurement point tool: - **Front Palm Length:** Press **Shift** to constrain measurement vertically; double-click to finish. The measurement appears in the object window, including code and size data from the pattern board. - **Width Measurements:** Measure from the top to the end of the board to get widths such as chest or front width. If a measured line shows as a virtual line with zero size, switch to the edit tool, right-click the measurement line, and select "Display Length" to correct it. - **Constrain Directions:** Press **Shift** to constrain measurements vertically or horizontally. Use the middle mouse button and left mouse button to adjust the board's direction or position for precise measurement alignment. --- ## Precise Positioning and Texture Switching To achieve precise positioning on the pattern board: - Press **Start**, then use the **right mouse button** to move the pattern. - Click the specific data input window to enter exact values, then confirm with **OK**. - Texture surfaces can be toggled: switch between the previous point’s texture and the black-and-white surface to aid visual alignment. --- ## Measuring Outside Board Lengths and Curves Press **P key** to switch to measuring the outside length of the board, indicated by a blue pointer. - Operations remain consistent: single-click to start and end measurements. - The free sewing tool functions similarly for curve measurement. - Example: Measure the length of the T-stitch embroidery mountain curve.

chunks.content: - Texture surfaces can be toggled: switch between the previous point’s texture and the black-and-white surface to aid visual alignment. --- ## Measuring Outside Board Lengths and Curves Press **P key** to switch to measuring the outside length of the board, indicated by a blue pointer. - Operations remain consistent: single-click to start and end measurements. - The free sewing tool functions similarly for curve measurement. - Example: Measure the length of the T-stitch embroidery mountain curve. Additional curve measurement tools include the **hook and loop tool**: - Select the pre-sew dragon curve, right-click to set it as a measurement point, and measure its length. - Switching between measurement types (straight line, X-shape, Y-shape) is possible via the edit measurement tool’s menu. --- ## Displaying and Hiding Measurement Data in 2D and 3D Views Measurement lines and values appear as corresponding lines on the 3D garment model. - Users can toggle visibility in the garment information display: - Hide/show in 2D size display - Hide/show in 3D size display - The object window lists measurements as "length of a 3D line." --- ## Understanding Differences Between 2D and 3D Measurement Lengths Length differences between 2D and 3D lines arise due to garment simulation effects: - Fabric stretch under gravity - Artificial structure of the garment - Model wearing the garment causing deformation These factors cause the 3D garment to deviate from flat 2D measurements. --- ## Storing and Reusing Measurement Data Measurement data can be saved and reused to improve efficiency: - After editing, click the **storage button** in the upper right of the object window to save measurements as a CSV file. - The CSV file can be opened and edited in office software for review. - When measuring new styles, open the saved CSV to automatically load previous measurement positions, eliminating the need to re-enter them. - Select positions in the measurement point window, confirm the selection, and measure as usual. --- ## Adding New Measurement Positions and Applying Data - New measurement points can be added by clicking directly in the measurement window and filling in the position before measuring. - The **apply button** at the bottom allows selection of measurement data to fill into the required fields or columns automatically. --- ## Summary CLO2024.1 enhances the measurement point functionality with flexible line and curve measurement modes, precise positioning tools, comprehensive editing options, and efficient data storage and reuse. These improvements aid accurate garment measurement workflows in both 2D and 3D environments.
